requiredObligationsRetainedForEachChild: appropriate control samples and own raw measurement records
valid calibration OR reaction stoichiometry appropriate to the chosen method
ascorbicCompetency: Select, plan, carry out and evaluate a controlled ascorbic-acid quantitative assay; redox activity can justify iodometric stoichiometry, but other reducing substances require controls or a suitable more-selective method.
parabenCompetency: Select, plan, carry out and evaluate a controlled quantitative assay of one specified p-hydroxybenzoic acid ester; for calibrated chromatographic measurement, distinguish retention time, peak area and concentration and establish selectivity and working range.
independentMasteryCounterexamples: Successful ascorbic control/stoichiometry with failure to distinguish peak retention time from paraben concentration.
Successful paraben calibration/re-dilution with failure to control extra reducing-agent consumption in ascorbic titration.
fullCase1: Own actual assays of both analytes plus separate supplementary calculations; original ascorbic content1690.752mg/L and paraben content50mg/L. Neither a calculation alone nor the second analyte substitutes for actual execution.
fullCase2: Actual fresh remeasurement of both analytes; separate redox matrix interference and paraben out-of-range dilution, no required integrated comparison conclusion.
sources: HEQ1.5B04 supports quantitative ascorbic determination; HEB05 concerns paraben USE and belongs to0d59, not full normative paraben assay. Other jurisdiction/course roles must be retained and authored analytical transfer declared.
